findings.highlight: I’ll relax in this familiar club room
findings.evidenceJa: 夕方までまったりしよう
findings.governingReading: relax in the familiar clubroom until evening
findings.explanation: The intended duration of Shirou and Saber’s stay disappears.

findings.highlight: I’m going to go teach
findings.evidenceJa: 稽古をつけてくる
findings.governingReading: go give the students practice or instruction
findings.explanation: Taiga’s active martial coaching is generalized.

findings.highlight: you can relax here
findings.evidenceJa: ここでぼけっとしてなさい
findings.governingReading: stay here and space out
findings.explanation: Taiga’s teasing order becomes neutral permission.

findings.highlight: if you want to shoot
findings.evidenceJa: 弓を持ちたくなったら
findings.governingReading: if he feels like taking up a bow
findings.explanation: The desire to handle or resume the bow is prematurely made actual shooting.

findings.highlight: …Yeah, she’s not wrong.
findings.evidenceJa: 確かに、矢を射るという事において自分はどの部員よりも巧いだろう
findings.governingReading: the source moves directly from silence into Shirou’s internal assessment of his shooting ability
findings.explanation: mirror moon inserts an explicit agreement absent from the source.

findings.highlight: my everyday training in magic
findings.evidenceJa: 毎夜日課になっている魔術の鍛錬
findings.governingReading: magecraft training performed as a nightly routine
findings.explanation: The nightly schedule and ritualized routine are generalized.

findings.highlight: I don’t know if I’ll even hit the target
findings.evidenceJa: 会心に入れるかも怪しい
findings.governingReading: he doubts he can even enter the state of kai or unified heart
findings.explanation: A named archery mental state is mistranslated as the physical result of hitting.

findings.highlight: The endurance is good enough if you’re training yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 弓を持たなくともちゃんと自身を鍛えているなら、それも立派な久の境地
findings.governingReading: proper self-training without holding a bow can itself constitute a fine state of kyū
findings.explanation: The principle is reduced to malformed English about endurance being “good enough.”

findings.highlight: it’s also good to try to respect archery
findings.evidenceJa: 弓に礼を尽くそうとする心も“拘り”よ
findings.governingReading: even the impulse to show the bow every courtesy is an attachment
findings.explanation: Taiga’s warning that reverence itself can bind Shirou is reversed into praise.

findings.highlight: It’ll all be good if you just nod
findings.evidenceJa: なんであれ絡まれば流れは淀む
findings.governingReading: whatever one becomes entangled in causes the flow to stagnate
findings.explanation: The central metaphor and causal warning disappear entirely.

findings.highlight: why the upset face
findings.evidenceJa: 難しい顔してんじゃん
findings.governingReading: he is wearing a difficult or pensive expression
findings.explanation: Thoughtful difficulty is recast as emotional upset.

findings.highlight: She told me not to worry too much
findings.evidenceJa: あんまり拘るなって叱られた
findings.governingReading: she scolded him not to become overly attached or fixated
findings.explanation: The philosophical theme of fixation is generalized into worry.

findings.highlight: you won’t understand the mentality if you can’t face yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 自身を射抜けない者にその精神は伝わらない
findings.governingReading: one who cannot face and pierce the self cannot receive that spirit
findings.explanation: Half of Ayako’s parallel condition and its archery metaphor disappear.

findings.highlight: the self that is shot to the target already knows “it will hit”, and the action and the result become one to make the past and the future into a point
findings.evidenceJa: 離れ行く自身、すでに“中る”事を知り、行為と結果、その順序が一体化し、過去と未来を点にする残心
findings.governingReading: in zanshin, the departing self already knows the hit; act, result, and their order unite, making past and future one point
findings.explanation: The English misassigns the self as shot at the target and renders the temporal doctrine in malformed syntax.

findings.highlight: a way to train yourself according to set stages
findings.evidenceJa: 儀礼、儀式にのっとった自己の鍛錬法
findings.governingReading: a method of self-training governed by rite and ritual
findings.explanation: The religious and ceremonial basis is replaced by generic procedural stages.

findings.highlight: meditation in magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術の瞑想
findings.governingReading: magecraft meditation
findings.explanation: A technical compound becomes vague English suggesting meditation performed inside magic.

findings.highlight: We shoot arrows and feel it when we hit the target
findings.evidenceJa: 矢を放って、それが中った時に、あ、きたって錯覚できる
findings.governingReading: when the released arrow strikes, they can experience the illusion of “there—it came”
findings.explanation: Ayako’s account of the illusory moment of arrival is flattened.

findings.highlight: we can’t tell if we succeeded unless the arrow hits the mark
findings.evidenceJa: 矢が中った事でしか自分が綺麗になれたのかが判らない
findings.governingReading: only the arrow’s hit tells them whether the self became beautiful or purified
findings.explanation: Spiritual self-refinement is replaced by generic success.

findings.highlight: they are only making the arrow hit the target with technique. Real shooting hits
findings.evidenceJa: それは“中ている”だけ。本当の射は“中る”のよ
findings.governingReading: that merely makes the arrow hit; true shooting arrives at a hit
findings.explanation: The written/ruby distinction between engineered hitting and a true shot’s natural hit is substantially flattened.

findings.highlight: I don’t know
findings.evidenceJa: そんな事はないけどな
findings.governingReading: that is not so
findings.explanation: Shirou’s direct rejection becomes uncertainty.

findings.highlight: I went to see how surprised you’d look
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対に動揺してるだろうって見に行ったら
findings.governingReading: she went over expecting him to be visibly shaken
findings.explanation: Ayako’s expectation of emotional disturbance is weakened to surprise.

findings.highlight: you were acting normally
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮は今まで通りだった
findings.governingReading: Emiya was exactly as he had always been
findings.explanation: Shirou’s actual unchanged state becomes a possibly performed normality.

findings.highlight: you said
findings.evidenceJa: しれっと言う
findings.governingReading: he said it with perfect nonchalance
findings.explanation: Shirou’s unnerving matter-of-fact delivery disappears.

findings.highlight: I missed because I imagined for it to miss
findings.evidenceJa: いや、今のは外れるイメージだったから外したんだ
findings.governingReading: he missed because the image he held was one of missing
findings.explanation: The English uses a malformed infinitive construction.

findings.highlight: You’ve reached nothingness
findings.evidenceJa: 武道でいうところの無の境地だろう
findings.governingReading: what martial arts call the state of no-mind
findings.explanation: A technical state of emptied consciousness becomes metaphysical nothingness.

findings.highlight: You’ve reached nothingness
findings.evidenceJa: それって自然と一体化してるってコトだ。武道でいうところの無の境地だろう
findings.governingReading: that means being one with nature—the state martial arts call no-mind
findings.explanation: An interpretive categorization is promoted into a claim that Shirou has definitively attained it.

findings.highlight: I can nod back to the nothingness part
findings.evidenceJa: 無の境地に関しては頷ける
findings.governingReading: the part about the state of no-mind makes sense to him
findings.explanation: A cognition idiom is translated as a literal and unidiomatic nod back.

findings.highlight: erase oneself to make the self into a circuit
findings.evidenceJa: 自己を消して一つの『回路』になる
findings.governingReading: erase the self and become one single circuit
findings.explanation: The self-erasure transformation is rendered with redundant, awkward agency.

findings.highlight: It is the strength of a magus
findings.evidenceJa: 力の証だ
findings.governingReading: is proof of a magus’s power
findings.explanation: Evidence of power becomes the power itself.

findings.highlight: transparent because you’re unselfish
findings.evidenceJa: 無欲だから透けやすい
findings.governingReading: easy to become transparent because he is desireless
findings.explanation: A lack of personal desire is moralized into altruistic unselfishness.

findings.highlight: You have to know how to have fun now
findings.evidenceJa: 若いうちにハメを外しておかないと
findings.governingReading: he must cut loose while still young
findings.explanation: Transgressive release from restraint is softened into ordinary fun.

findings.highlight: People call those kinds of people good-for-nothings, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: わかって？　なんて、ガラにもなく上品に付け足してくる
findings.governingReading: she adds an uncharacteristically elegant “understand?”
findings.explanation: Ayako’s self-conscious shift in register and its narration disappear.

findings.highlight: Why are you so worried about me?
findings.evidenceJa: なんだってそこまで俺に構うんだよ
findings.governingReading: why does she fuss over or concern herself with him so much?
findings.explanation: Ayako’s active interference and attention become private worry.

findings.highlight: We were all laughing
findings.evidenceJa: みんなで騒いでた時
findings.governingReading: when everyone was making merry together
findings.explanation: The broader noisy social scene is narrowed to laughter.

findings.highlight: She declares as if smiling to a rival
findings.evidenceJa: ライバルに笑いかけるように、美綴綾子はそう言った
findings.governingReading: Ayako says it as though smiling at a rival
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically awkward and weakens the personal competitive warmth.

findings.highlight: You’re my student and you’re better than most people.
findings.evidenceJa: 士郎はわたしの教え子だし、人一倍成ってるんだから
findings.governingReading: Shirou is Taiga’s pupil and has developed or matured exceptionally well, especially in the relevant archery context.
findings.explanation: ‘Better than most people’ turns 成ってる, a more contextual statement of being well formed or accomplished, into a generic ranking claim. It also weakens Taiga’s proud teacherly appraisal.

findings.highlight: It’s true that I’m better than anyone when it comes to shooting arrows.
findings.evidenceJa: 確かに、矢を射るという事において自分はどの部員よりも巧いだろう。
findings.governingReading: Shirou is probably more skilled than any club member specifically in shooting arrows.
findings.explanation: The English removes だろう’s modest uncertainty and broadens どの部員よりも (‘than any club member’) into ‘better than anyone.’ It makes Shirou’s self-assessment categorical and universal.

findings.highlight: Even though I was away for a while, I’m sure I could get the same result I had when I used to come here.
findings.evidenceJa: たとえ弓から離れていても、今すぐに現役の頃の結果を出せると思う。
findings.governingReading: Even while separated from the bow, Shirou thinks he could immediately produce the results he achieved when he was active.
findings.explanation: ‘Away for a while’ changes being away from the bow into being absent from the club for a period. The source’s point is that his present magical training lets him shoot without currently holding or practicing with a bow.

findings.highlight: there will be more dripping water the more water the cup holds.
findings.evidenceJa: これはグラスが重ければ重いほど蛇口の栓が開かれていくのです。
findings.governingReading: The more weight or water the glass contains, the farther the faucet’s stopper opens.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the valve-opening mechanism with a generic claim that more water simply drips out. The source establishes a reserve-dependent control system, not just a larger output proportional to volume.

findings.highlight: You can get into the mentality without the bow, so I was annoyed that the bow might just be hindering you.
findings.evidenceJa: というか弓を持たなくても会心に入れるんだから、むしろ弓なんて邪魔じゃないってムカついたもんよ
findings.governingReading: Because Shirou can enter kai even without holding the bow, Ayako was annoyed that the bow itself might be an unnecessary hindrance to him.
findings.explanation: ‘Get into the mentality’ turns the specific archery state 会 into a generic mental attitude. The point is that Shirou can reach the formal state of the shot without equipment, not merely think in the right mood.

findings.highlight: Shooting is the mentality of shooting your mind, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 射っていうのはさ、自分を射抜く精神でしょ。
findings.governingReading: The act of shooting is a state of mind in which one pierces oneself, according to Ayako’s explanation.
findings.explanation: ‘The mentality of shooting your mind’ is unidiomatic and changes 射抜く (pierce/shoot through) into the nonsensical image of firing at one’s mind. The self-piercing metaphor is obscured.

findings.highlight: She simply discards all the chaotic events that happened since last night, and I feel like it’s just a normal day.
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜からジェットコースターのように繰り広げられた出来事が、この人の一声でぐるんと日常にひっくり返るんだから。
findings.governingReading: The events that have unfolded like a roller coaster since last night are flipped around into ordinary life by a single word from Taiga.
findings.explanation: ‘Discards’ changes a sudden world-reversing intervention into passive dismissal, and the English removes the roller-coaster image and the active flip back into normality. ‘I feel like’ makes the transformation only Shirou’s impression.

findings.highlight: I gave up my day off to teach my students.
findings.evidenceJa: 今日も今日とて、お休み返上して教え子の面倒みてるんだから
findings.governingReading: As usual, Taiga has given up her day off to look after or take care of her pupils.
findings.explanation: ‘Teach my students’ narrows 面倒みてる to instruction and drops 今日も今日とて, the comic suggestion that she routinely spends days off caring for pupils. The teacher-as-caretaker characterization is weakened.

findings.highlight: There are no robbers or fires here. You can rest assured and go back to your club.
findings.evidenceJa: こっちには火事も泥棒もサーカスも来てないから、安心して部活動に励んでくれ
findings.governingReading: There have been no fires, robbers, or circuses here, so Taiga can devote herself to club activities in peace.
findings.explanation: The English drops the absurd ‘circus’ from the escalating list and turns 励んでく, apply yourself to club activity, into simply going back to the club. Both the joke and mock-formal register are weakened.

findings.highlight: I’m calling you, so it’ll be terrible if you hang up without hearing me out!
findings.evidenceJa: 恥をしのいでお姉ちゃんが電話してるっていうのに、用件も聞かずにきったらタイヘンなんだからー！
findings.governingReading: Taiga’s ‘big sister’ is enduring or swallowing her shame to make the call, so hanging up without hearing the purpose would be disastrous.
findings.explanation: The English deletes both the shame she is enduring and her self-styled ‘big sister’ address, removing the setup for Shirou’s next reflection on the phrasing.

findings.highlight: Well, I guess she’s in a little trouble right now too.
findings.evidenceJa: そもそも恥を忍ばず凌いでいるあたり、藤ねえ的にライブで小ピンチなのか。
findings.governingReading: Shirou riffs on the shame expression and infers that, by Taiga’s standards, she is in a small immediate crisis.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the wording-based joke and presents generic trouble as the entire thought. It also removes the comic ‘live’/right-now framing and the tentative inference.

findings.highlight: “That’ll be it for my order. I want it delivered to the archery range right away. Bye.”
findings.evidenceJa: 以上、注文おわり。至急弓道部まで届けられたし。カチリ
findings.governingReading: Taiga abruptly ends her formal order and hangs up with a click.
findings.explanation: ‘Bye’ replaces カチリ, the spoken or represented click of the phone being hung up. The mechanical abruptness of Taiga’s demand is replaced by an ordinary farewell.

findings.highlight: That is the time that requires the most attention. I shall be on standby, right next to you.
findings.evidenceJa: 睡眠中など最も警護すべき対象です。当然、シロウの側で私も待機しますが
findings.governingReading: Sleep is when Shirou is the object most in need of guarding, so Saber will naturally stand by at his side.
findings.explanation: ‘Requires the most attention’ removes the explicit protected-object framing of 警護すべき対象. Saber’s professional duty to guard Shirou becomes a generic claim about a demanding time.

findings.highlight: This is what it means to fight alongside her!
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーと一緒に戦う、ってコトはつまりそういうコトじゃないか……！
findings.governingReading: Shirou flusteredly realizes that fighting alongside Saber means, in other words, this constant proximity and guard arrangement, doesn’t it?
findings.explanation: The English turns a rhetorical, embarrassed inference into a categorical exclamation. It makes Shirou sound certain about what fighting together means rather than horrified by the implication he has just noticed.
